sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Supply of Drummed and Bagged Penetration Grade Bitumen

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified Roman-law tradition, Napoleonic Code heritage, strong EU-law primacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China-Luxembourg Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTA, signed 12 March 1994, in force 1995)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU)-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984, in force 1986)
Luxembourg-United States Tax Convention (1996, as amended by 2004, 2009, and 2023 protocols)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MAC, 2015)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (Pillar Two, 15% minimum tax)
EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - Freedom of Establishment (Art. 49 TFEU) and Capital Movements (Art. 63 TFEU)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended by Laws of 25 March 2020 and 20 July 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE, 'Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs') transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the RBE; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access suspended following CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022, Case C-37/20; full access restricted to FIU 'CRF', CSSF, tax authorities, notaries, and obliged entities demonstrating a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Biometric passport certified copies of all managers and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil registry/immigration authority of each UBO's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if origin is an Apostille Convention state) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states), plus sworn French translation if not in French/English/German

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of any corporate shareholder (non-resident parent entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or competent registrar of the parent company's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated competent authority of the parent's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association (statuts) and board resolutions of the corporate shareholder(s) approving the Luxembourg SARL incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) authorizing the Luxembourg notary and local counsel to incorporate the SARL, sign the deed, and appoint the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, plus certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds declaration and UBO organizational chart, stamped and held by Luxembourg AML counsel (file-opened pre-incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg law firm / advising notary (internal KYC attestation; no foreign authentication required)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal AML due-diligence record only; not subject to apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, managers, UBOs, and material counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and (EU) No 833/2014), the OFAC SDN List (mandatory given USD-denominated SWIFT LC/TT payment rails), and the Luxembourg CRF (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) guidance. PEP identification and enhanced due diligence apply per FATF Recommendations 12 and the Law of 12 November 2004, including PEPs in any foreign jurisdiction and close associates/family members. Ongoing transaction monitoring, adverse-media checks, and duty to file suspicion reports (STR/SAR) to the CRF are governed by CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online platform www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be expressed in Latin-alphabet characters; French is the prevailing statutory drafting language, although German and English names may be accepted where clearly distinguishable. The legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' is mandatory and must appear in the corporate name as registered. Foreign-language trading names (e.g., English) are permitted only as secondary trading designations and do not replace the French RCS legal name. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS entries and must not breach public policy or protected terms. No local-script transliteration is required since Luxembourg uses the Latin alphabet exclusively.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Banquier, Caisse d'Epargne (reserved for licensed credit institutions; requires CSSF authorization)
Assurance, Assureur, Réassurance, Courtier d'Assurance (reserved for regulated insurance/brokerage entities; requires CAA authorization)
SICAV, FCP, Fonds de Pension, OPCVM, Fonds d'Investissement (reserved for regulated investment funds/products; requires CSSF authorization)
Bourse, Marché Réglementé, Chambre de Compensation (reserved for regulated market operators)
État, Commune, Administration, Ministère (tokens implying public authority; requires ministerial concession)
Croix-Rouge, Croissant-Rouge, and any Geneva-Convention-protected emblems
Union Européenne, Luxembourg for Finance, or any words implying official EU/Luxembourg sponsorship without prior authorization
English/foreign legal-form suffixes such as INC, PLC, LLC, LLP (not permissible as the primary RCS legal-form designation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be resubmitted in amended form immediately via the LBR/RCS portal. Formal administrative appeal must be lodged with the RCS Registrar in writing within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice, stating the legal basis for distinctiveness under the Law of 10 August 1915 and RCS administrative practice. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, judicial recourse lies with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement, Commercial Chamber) under the general rules of the Code of Civil Procedure. Practically, the efficient path for time-sensitive incorporations is to file a revised name rather than pursue administrative appeal, since name review is typically completed within 3-5 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. Domiciliation companies licensed under the Law of 31 May 1999 may supply the statutory seat (siège statutaire) and corporate mailbox in Luxembourg. However, the SARL must maintain genuine administrative substance in Luxembourg, including local central management decisions, board meeting minutes, accounting records, corporate records, and a Luxembourg bank account, to sustain Luxembourg tax residency under L.I.R. Article 159 and to avoid reclassification as fiscally resident elsewhere. Pure virtual mail-drop arrangements without local substance are not permissible for this wholesale trading activity and will jeopardize VAT registration, customs facilitation, and banking KYC acceptance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate: estimated 25-35% annual probability of an unannounced on-site verification by the RCS Registrar, tax authorities (Administration des Contributions Directes), or CSSF-sanctioned inspectors where the company is non-resident-owned and trades in containerized goods. The probability increases to circa 50-55% if the registered office is a shared multi-client domiciliation address, if no local employee or director is physically present in Luxembourg, or if the company has significant turnover with no matching local substance. Conversely, a substance-rich SARL with local director(s), office, and independent records faces an estimated 10-15% inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and availability verification at LBR/RCS (single name reservation application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fee schedule (per reservation application)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte notarié constitutif) including notary KYC/AML checks and preparation of statuts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff schedule under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on notarial fees, plus statutory disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS commercial registration filing (immatriculation au RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR single-event incorporation filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation in RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic publication tariff per entry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO filing at the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fee per initial UBO declaration (flat, independent of number of UBOs disclosed)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents (passports, powers of attorney, certificates of good standing, articles of association) - estimated 5 documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consular post of each document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document fee schedule of the issuing state (typically USD 30-100 per apostille; excludes courier)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translations of foreign corporate documents by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (approx. EUR 35 per 100 words for 8-12 estimated pages)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/CFT due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, and corporate-structure advisory by Luxembourg counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee (EUR 2,500-3,200) inclusive of commercial sanctions-database subscription

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation agreement with a licensed domiciliation company (first-year fee, including registered office and mail handling)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (agréée under the Law of 31 May 1999)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (EUR 1,800-4,000 per annum for a standard trading SARL)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration and activation of Luxembourg business number (eCDF) for VAT and income-tax purposes
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration des contributions directes / Administration de l'enregistrement (via eCDF portal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; automatic upon RCS registration and online eCDF activation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for consular legalization of Luxembourg-issued corporate excerpts for downstream foreign counterparties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs and destination-country consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency provision; official per-document consular fee (USD 80-150 typical)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Chapter 5, Articles 180 et seq. (S.à r.l. regime), as reformed by the Law of 23 June 2016 and the Law of 23 September 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 19 December 2008 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice, operating through the electronic portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif notarié) incorporating the articles of association (statuts), filed electronically with the RCS on www.lbr.lu and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum fully paid-up share capital, subscribed and paid in cash or in kind upon incorporation; cash contributions must be evidenced by a bank certificate (attestation bancaire de blocage) issued to the company in formation or by a deposit into the notary's escrow account (compte séquestre); funds remain blocked until the RCS registration; capital duty (droit d'apport) abolished as of 1 January 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the articles of association submitted by the founder are adopted and the subscribed shares are fully paid up as evidenced by the bank certificate issued to the company in formation; that the registered office of the company be and is hereby established at [●] in Luxembourg; that [●] be and is hereby appointed as Manager (Gérant) with authority to act alone, and the Chairman is instructed to file all statutory documents with the Luxembourg Business Registers and to arrange publication in the RESA; that the Manager be authorized to open bank accounts, to execute trading contracts, and to complete VAT, social security and beneficial-owner registrations; and that all prior acts of the promoters are hereby ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and negative certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS, online name reservation service at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application for reservation of the proposed company name, submitting two or three alternative names in descending order of preference. The RCS verifies conformity with the Law of 10 August 1915, including distinctiveness, absence of confusion with existing Luxembourg or protected Community trademarks, and mandatory inclusion of the words 'société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' The negative certificate validates exclusive use of the name.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Copy of national ID or passport of the applicant founder
Certificate of criminal record (casier judiciaire) of the proposed manager
Draft articles of association (statuts)
Notarized power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File revised alternative names within 5 business days; contest a refusal before the competent district court pursuant to Article 22-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 if grounds of distinctiveness are wrongly assessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked capital deposit and bank attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorized by the CSSF, or the escrow account (compte séquestre) of the drafting notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the S.à r.l. in formation and deposit the full minimum share capital of EUR 12,000. Obtain a bank attestation (attestation de blocage) confirming the deposit and the irrevocable blocking of funds pending delivery of the RCS registration certificate. Release instructions are given solely upon production of the registration extract.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC questionnaires
Proof of identity and residential address of each founder
Draft articles of association
Source of funds declaration and bank references
Company in formation name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank onboarding exceeds timeline, deposit the capital with the notary's escrow account; the notary's receipt (récépissé de consignation) substitutes for the bank certificate and is accepted by the RCS and the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation and statutory registration duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary for execution of the notarial deed of incorporation and the articles of association. The notary verifies legal capacity, lawful corporate object, paid-up capital evidence and compliance with the civil law formalities; the deed is then presented to the AEDT for the fixed registration duty and a certified copy (expédition) is issued for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate of name reservation
Bank certificate of blocked paid-up capital or notary escrow receipt
Draft articles of association signed by all founders
Identity documents and criminal records of the initial managers
Statement of the registered office address (siège social)
For legal entity founders: excerpt from home register and resolution authorizing incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any typing or substantive error is cured by a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) passed before the same notary; if the notary raises AML concerns, supply the requested source-of-funds evidence and re-execute the deed without loss of priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS, electronic filing at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed and the application for registration (immatriculation) electronically to the RCS. The RCS performs a legality review of the deed and filings; upon approval the company is registered, receives its RCS number, and the registration notice is published in the RESA, conferring legal personality and third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: Certified copy (expédition) of the notarial deed of incorporation
Signed application for registration (Formulaire de demande d'immatriculation)
Proof of payment of the RCS registration fee
Identity documents and specimen signatures of the managers
Consent of the landlord and lease abstract for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any query (demande de complément) within one month with corrected or supplementary documentation and re-submit electronically; the company acquires legal personality only upon registration, so any administrative delay is mitigated by using the priority filing queue of the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner, VAT and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration with the RBE within one month of registration, identifying any individual ultimately owning or controlling the S.à r.l.; apply to the AEDT for the Luxembourg VAT number using the official form; enroll the company with the CCSS for the manager's and any employees' social security; notify the local commune of the business activity if any physical premises are occupied.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and extract
RBE declaration form listing each beneficial owner with percentage of capital and control
VAT registration form (Formulaire 640) and jurisdiction of establishment statement
CCSS registration form and employment status of the manager
Lease agreement of the registered office
Company bank account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filings are subject to administrative fines; submit rectified or supplementary declarations promptly if the RBE or AEDT requests clarification; a refusal of VAT registration is remedied by petitioning the AEDT with the full incorporation file and evidence of economic activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie, des nouvelles technologies et de la recherche; communal authority (administration communale) of the place of establishment for any exploitation permit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial license for pure wholesale trading; where a physical storage depot is operated, the communal exploitation permit (autorisation d'exploitation) under the Law of 9 May 2014 on the environmental permitting of classified installations (commodo-incommodo) applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of Luxembourg), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 4 – simple declaration (déclaration) for covered warehousing of drummed and bagged bitumen products; a full environmental impact assessment is not triggered below the Annex II thresholds of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and the nominal storage volumes do not meet Seveso III classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater generated by pure wholesale trading; any stormwater runoff from a paved handling yard must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 June 1994 on groundwater protection: pH 6.5-8.5, suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 10 mg/L; no VOC emissions arise from sealed containerized storage; waste bitumen and empty drums are managed under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management with European Waste Codes 17 03 02 and 15 01 10 as applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the Service National de la Protection Civile (SNPC) and the communal fire brigade; structural load and racking stability inspection by an approved control body (organisme de contrôle agréé, e.g., Seco Luxembourg or SOCOTEC); workplace occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering manual handling, forklift operations, personal protective equipment and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect tax; Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; Luxembourg Customs and Excise Agency (Administration des douanes et accises) for import/export formalities. Central e-portal: myguichet.lu; tax portals: impotsdirects.public.lu and aedt.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-established foreign entity must submit the Luxembourg VAT registration form (specifically the form for taxable persons not established in Luxembourg, referencing Form 102 or the equivalent EIC procedure) through the MyGuichet.lu electronic portal, together with certified copies of the constitutive documents, proof of the foreign VAT identification number, and appointment of a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) where the foreign entity has no permanent establishment and no EU VAT identity in another Member State. The AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits within approximately 10 to 15 business days. In parallel, the SARL obtains a Luxembourg national registration number (numéro de matricule) from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and is registered ex officio with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a resident Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) is a corporate taxpayer fully subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax on worldwide income and assets, subject to tax treaties, the participation exemption for qualifying shareholdings, and the ATAD-compliant interest limitation rules. The SARL is not eligible for pass-through taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections: (1) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (2) option to subject real property transactions to VAT rather than registration duties; (3) election for a commercial company to be tax-transparent only for the specific partnership forms (SCS, SCSp); (4) article 164 group taxation election for certain integrated domestic corporate groups; (5) hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply mandatorily with no elective opt-out, although entity classification disalignment with foreign jurisdictions can be mitigated through the Luxembourg entity choice (e.g., SCS/SCSp transparent vs. SARL corporate).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), compliant with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual net turnover (exclusive of VAT) for the Luxembourg small enterprise exemption applicable only to taxpayers established in Luxembourg; a non-established foreign supplier has no de minimis threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT before effecting any taxable supply of goods or services in Luxembourg; the EUR 10,000 Union-wide distance sales threshold applies to online/remote sales of goods under the OSS procedure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no general B2B electronic invoicing mandate and no real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control system. Invoices may be issued electronically (PDF/A-XML, EDI, or other formats) subject to authenticity of origin and integrity of content under the VAT invoicing rules. Mandatory e-invoicing applies exclusively to suppliers of Luxembourg public contracting authorities through the PEPPOL BIS format. VAT returns (monthly or quarterly), the recapitulative EU sales list (RE), and Intrastat declarations are filed electronically via the Luxembourg tax authorities' e-filing platforms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate is available under Article 41 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for export supplies of goods (including containerized drums and bags of penetration grade bitumen) dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods physically leave the EU under a complete customs export declaration, the supplier retains credible transport and trade documentation, and, where the buyer is an EU-established counterparty, the intra-Community supply qualifies under Article 42 with the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and the supply is included in the recapitulative statement. Zero-rating for intra-EU business-to-business supplies requires the goods to be dispatched from Luxembourg to another EU Member State and the customer to communicate a valid VAT ID; such supply remains subject to proof of transport within the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration (Single Administrative Document / electronic declaration) lodged in the Export Control System (ECS/ICS-AES) and validated by Luxembourg Customs or the customs office of exportation in the Member State of departure
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent multimodal transport document (CMR for road, sea waybill, air waybill) evidencing dispatch and physical exit from the European Union
Commercial Invoice and Packing List identifying the goods (ISIC 4661, bitumen/asphalt products), quantities, container numbers, and Incoterms
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 payment evidence demonstrating receipt of export proceeds on the seller's Luxembourg bank account
Luxembourg VAT return (Form TVA) and recapitulative EU sales list (Form RE) showing the zero-rated supply and, where applicable, Intrastat declaration for intra-EU movements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs conduct joint risk-based audits of export traders that systematically claim zero-rated supplies. Documentary deficiencies, mismatched Incoterms, warehouse intermediaries without physical movement, or failure to evidence receipt of export proceeds within the commercial payment term (typically indistinguishable from the 180-day documentary credit/telegraphic transfer benchmark) can trigger a retroactive reassessment of the supply at 17% VAT, denial of input VAT deduction on related purchasing costs, and the withdrawal of zero-rated refunds. Statutory consequences include default interest at the Luxembourg statutory rate, administrative fines between EUR 250 and EUR 10,000 per infringement under Article 71 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, and criminal fiscal fraud sanctions under the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), including imprisonment in aggravated cases, joint and several liability of directors, and publication of the corrective tax assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank and euro-area implementing arm of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential banking supervision is co-administered by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993; economic sanctions and capital-movement prohibitions are enforced via EU Regulations and the Luxembourg law implementing the AML/CFT framework of 27 May 2022.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full eurozone member with unrestricted capital-account and current-account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU and the BCL Organic Law of 23 December 1998. The euro is freely convertible; there is no national foreign-exchange control, no prior authorization for inbound or outbound payments, and no barrier to profit remittance by an SARL. Practical constraints are fiscal and documentary only: dividend withholding tax (0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 2011/96/EU for qualifying corporate shareholders, 5% to 15% under double tax treaties, or 15% at the domestic rate to non-qualifying non-residents), net wealth tax good-standing, and the CSSF-mandated AML/KYC verification of each treasury movement. USD bitumen receipts may therefore flow freely into EUR accounts or remain in USD at the SARL treasury's discretion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law does not impose export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratios, repatriation timelines, or a statutory obligation to convert USD receipts to EUR. Banks must nevertheless provide the BCL with balance-of-payments statistical classification on each cross-border transfer and, as a matter of CSSF practice, request a purpose identification statement; no substantive compliance burden is placed on the trading SARL beyond accurate remittance reference fields.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (pre-incorporation blocked capital deposit) and EUR/USD Operational Treasury Account with documentary guarantee facility
Operational Multi-Currency Account, USD clearing corridor, and Commodity Trade Finance line (import/export LC and DLC discounting)
Multi-currency Operational Account, Commercial Letter of Credit issuing account, and FX forward settlement account
Operational Account with export negotiation facilities and supplier payment rails

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EUR Domestic Settlement and escrow account (state-owned, conservative on commodity exposure)
Cross-border settlement and short-term treasury deposit account
Correspondent clearing and EUR corridor account (corporate product scope subject to continuing EMEA restructuring)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with material reservations. Luxembourg recognizes CSSF-authorised and passported EEA electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions (PIs) that may lawfully execute account-to-account MT103-equivalent settlement and issue payment cards on an SARL treasury account. However, an EMI/PI is legally barred from granting credit, opening trade documentary credits, negotiating letters of credit, or holding banking deposits. For a containerized bitumen wholesale operation requiring commercial LCs, supplier guarantees, and USD correspondent clearing above EUR 500,000 per event, an EMI is suitable only as a supplementary ancillary-collection and contingency-payment wallet; it is not a compliant substitute for a Tier-1 bank. Legal constraints include safeguarding obligations, transaction limits, adverse counterparty rating perception, and exclusion from BCL TARGET2 direct participation. Feasibility is therefore rated Medium for fringe treasury uses and Low as the primary banking rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and a live KYC interview are effectively mandatory. All Luxembourg Tier-1 commercial banks require at least one authorised director and each ultimate beneficial owner to attend either an in-person interview at the bank's Luxembourg head office or a certified secure video-identification session with simultaneous production of original documents. Fully remote account opening without a Luxembourg corporate introduction is systematically declined, and commodity-trading profiles are subjected to heightened due diligence. The SARL is also expected to demonstrate real local substance (registered office, lease, payroll, physical board minutes) before mandate execution is approved; banks commonly require a physical signature session for the account mandate conferring disbursement powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned counterpart or high-risk trade corridor detected in the bitumen supply chain, including cargo routing through sanctioned ports or transshipment jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening reports for directors, UBOs and all commercial counterparties; Luxembourg RBE register extract; customs CTU container packing certificate; full set of commercial contracts with incoterms; bill of lading with container and seal numbers; certificate of origin; refinery certificate of analysis for penetration-grade bitumen; cargo insurance policy; shipment tracking log; and a written compliance risk assessment signed by the appointed Luxembourg AML advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance mismatch flagged as letterbox risk because management decisions and operational services are not demonstrably located in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised lease of the Luxembourg head office; payroll records and Luxembourg social-security filings; board and shareholder minutes physically signed in Luxembourg; bank statements evidencing operational rather than pass-through flows; corporate income tax and VAT filings demonstrating local activity; an internal substance-mapping memo showing that commercial negotiation and treasury policy functions are exercised in Luxembourg; and an auditor's letter confirming physical presence and governance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain with layered intermediate holding companies preventing identification of the final natural persons
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully annotated organisational chart from each ultimate individual to the LU SARL; certified shareholders' register and issued registered-share certificates; RBE declaration confirmation; constitutional documents of every intermediate vehicle; notarial deeds and blocked capital contribution receipts; sworn statements of beneficial ownership; and source-of-wealth memoranda for each UBO supported by banking references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators such as invoice pricing diverging from market benchmarks or payment wiring defying the stated commercial flow
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SGS or independent surveyor weight and quality certificates at load and discharge ports; Platts or ICIS bitumen benchmark price extracts for the shipment date; order-invoice-payment three-way reconciliation; TARGET2 or Fedwire tracking evidence; UETR reference in the SWIFT MT103; incoterms-specific cost breakdown; commercial invoice and packing list for drums and bags; and a signed officer certificate attesting that the underlying cargo is genuine wholesale bitumen.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds or unexplained rapid inbound capital flow prior to or immediately after account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders resolution approving the capital injection; notarial certificate of paid-up capital and bank blocker-account confirmation; bank reference letters and three months of transferor bank statements; audited financial statements of the parent shareholder; tax residence certificate of the parent; declaration of source of wealth; evidence that funds were debited from the remitter account before use; and a written purpose statement mapped to the operational plan for the containerized bitumen wholesale business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection must comply with the Luxembourg SARL constitution rules: minimum issued capital of EUR 12,010 fully subscribed and, for treasury credibility in a trading business, fully paid in cash. The routing is a SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer from the shareholder or corporate lender to the bank account of the LU SARL, whether a pre-incorporation blocker account or the post-incorporation operating account. Field 50K must show the registered legal name of the remitting shareholder; field 59 the full name, BCL code and IBAN of the LU SARL; field 70 must state precisely: Capital contribution pursuant to shareholders resolution dated DD/MM/YYYY, or alternatively Intercompany loan under Luxembourg treasury policy. The receiving Luxembourg bank will also require a balance-of-payments direct-investment classification (equity versus intercompany loan) and, under CSSF AML/CFT rules, the full corporate file: signed resolution, notarial deed of contribution, UBO declarations, sanctions and PEP screening, certified charter, and evidence of economic substance. No FX-control approval is necessary; the bank simply verifies statutory purpose, clears the credit via TARGET2, and issues a credit confirmation suitable for audit and notarial file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlements for outbound trade disbursements rely on three clearing rails: (i) open-account telegraphic transfer via SWIFT MT103 for payments to bitumen suppliers and logistics providers, with the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) enabled for full traceability; (ii) MT202 COV for interbank cover payments where a USD correspondent leg is required; and (iii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued by a Luxembourg or counterparty bank using MT700/MT710 messages, with the SARL acting as beneficiary on resale or as applicant on purchase. Every containerized shipment file must contain the commercial invoice, full set of clean on-board bills of lading with container and seal numbers, certificate of analysis for the penetration-grade bitumen, packing list of drums and bags, certificate of origin, incoterms delivery evidence, cargo insurance certificate, and an independent surveyor's weight certificate. The paying or negotiating bank releases proceeds only against a complying presentation. EUR transfers settle value-dated through TARGET2; USD transfers clear via CHIPS or Fedwire through the bank's New York correspondent, with mandatory screening against EU, UN and US sanctions lists and retention of the payment purpose reference to demonstrate full auditability of the ISIC 4661 wholesale trade flow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD foreign-exchange forward contract with tenor up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or short-form FX Master Agreement with a CSSF-supervised Luxembourg bank; permitted exclusively for genuine trade-arising exposure on bitumen purchase or sales contracts.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) cash-settled in EUR on the USD/EUR exchange rate, legally permissible where a deliverable forward is illiquid or where counterparty limits require an NDF; internal policy shall prefer a deliverable forward where available.
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD) matching the repricing cycle of containerized bitumen inventory purchases and resale receivables; permitted with a signed Credit Support Annex and margin mechanics.
Purchased European-style foreign-exchange option (EUR call / USD put) for confirmed supply contracts, premium-based and strictly non-speculative, with no naked option writing by the treasury.

Natural FX hedging through multicurrency EUR/USD current accounts holding bitumen receipts and disbursements without derivative documentation, which remains the most supervisorily robust instrument for a low-risk standard wholesale profile.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filed via eCDF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end (shall be approved by shareholders within 6 months and filed within 1 month thereafter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal demand letter; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; publication of non-compliance; blocking of company filings; risk of judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return including net wealth tax and municipal business tax return (form 1, 2, 5)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD, Luxembourg tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the tax year if fiscal year is calendar year; otherwise within 6 months after fiscal year-end (extensions possible once granted)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Self-assessed late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; increase of tax by up to 10% for failure to file; additional penalties imposed by tax director may reach EUR 25,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner data (UBO registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Owners Register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE) operated under the Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the data as reflected on 15 February of the same year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 per failure to comply; possible criminal sanctions for repeated breaches; mandatory cross-check during RCS account filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of statutory registers and RCS data (exercise of shareholder rights and register audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS and notarial authorities (for SARL share transfers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediate update upon share transfer; no annual confirmation filing is separately required other than UBO confirmation by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or correct statutory registers invalidates transfer against the company; court sanctions and director liability; potential strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) for SARLs exceeding two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average 50 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 10 August 1915 and implementing regulations based on EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted or required for consolidated accounts, and allowed voluntarily for annual accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All SARLs must confirm the accuracy of beneficial owner data in the RBE by 31 March of each calendar year. Any share transfer changing beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register of transfers immediately after the notarized deed, and the RBE must be updated within one month of the transfer. The annual confirmation confirms all recorded transfers and the current holding shares are valid.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Options and Similar Rights

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,650 - USD 5,500 (typical annual domiciliation fee charged by Luxembourg corporate service providers)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 - USD 22,000 (typical certified audit fee range for a small or medium-sized commercial SARL)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined Luxembourg City rate of 24.94% (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT = 1.19% + municipal business tax 6.75% on the trade tax base)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; effective reliefs include: (1) participation exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains; (2) IP box regime granting 80% exemption on eligible IP-derived income (effective 4.99% rate on qualifying IP income); (3) 15% investment tax credit (taxe d'abattement) for qualifying new tangible assets; (4) 24% tax credit (super-deduction) for R&D wage expenditure; (5) special reserve for innovation (loi PCE).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (Formulaire 700) for CIT; Form 600 (Formulaire 600) for municipal business tax; e-filed via the RDE portal (Registre des déclarations électroniques) at myguichet.lu / ACD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (Article 164 LIR); calendar-year filers effective e-filing deadline administratively extended to 31 December of the year following the tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, Luxembourg business registration number (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), and matricule d'identification (Luxembourg tax ID)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies file through a Luxembourg tax representative; state the Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) address and the non-resident company's home registration particulars.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period under review
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Limited to the PE's accounting period; the PE must close its books on the same date as the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss per the statutory financial statements before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PE, allocate head-office attributable profits on an arm's-length basis (separate entity approach, OECD authorised OECD approach).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and hidden profit distributions (e.g., excessive management fees, non-arm's-length interest, fines, VAT penalties, portions of representation expenses) added back to the accounting profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reintegrate non-deductible expenses paid by the PE to the head office or to related foreign entities; apply Article 56 LIR arm's-length standard.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-deductible items, including municipal business tax paid, tax-exempt dividends qualifying for the participation exemption, IP box exempt portion (80%), and notional interest relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Participation exemption applies to qualifying PE-held shareholdings; the PE must substantiate the 10% holding (or purchase price) and 12-month holding condition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessment base before loss relief and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Luxembourg-source income allocable to the PE; DTA relief is claimed separately in the foreign home-country return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses (17-year carryforward) offset against the current-year taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE can carry forward its own Luxembourg PE losses for 17 years; losses of the foreign head office are not attributable to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss relief, subject to the progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 15%/17% CIT brackets; the lower 15% bracket (€175,000) and phase-out band apply to resident companies and PEs alike.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign PE tax credits (where the credit method applies under a treaty), withholding tax credits, investment credit (abattement), and one-off COVID/imputation credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are granted only on Luxembourg-source taxes; foreign-source PE income may be exempt under the relevant DTA and is not credited in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The municipal business tax is computed on the separately determined trade tax base (Formulaire 600); the solidarity surcharge is 7% of the CIT amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers (1) a formal reminder with a coercive fine of €10 to €100 per day, capped in practice; (2) administrative fine from €100 to €2,500 (Article 178 AO); (3) ex-officio assessment by the tax office with a 10% surcharge on the under-assessed tax; (4) late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on the outstanding tax; (5) criminal sanctions (fine up to €250,000, imprisonment) where the delay is part of fraudulent intent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (Article 148 LIR) on gross dividends; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) for a 10% parent holding, itself subject to a 12-month holding condition.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate (commonly 5% for ≥10% holdings, 15% for portfolio), the recipient must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the tax authority of its residence state. The Luxembourg paying entity files a relief-at-source request with the ACD (Bureau d'imposition) before the payment date, annexing the TRC, a certificate of shareholding, and a signed statement of beneficial ownership. Luxembourg applies the 'standard authorisation procedure' for EU/EEA parents (relief at source) and the 'refund procedure' where relief was not granted at source; refund claims must be filed with Form 700-B/refund (approval within 3 months).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: no WHT on royalties and no WHT on interest (except on profit-participating loans and certain payments to jurisdictions listed in the 2020 anti-hybrid/non-cooperative blacklist). Treaty DTA rates for interest (in the absence of an exemption) are typically 8–10%; royalty rates likewise 8–10% under older treaties, 0% under the Interest & Royalties Directive for EU related companies (25% minimum holding, permanent requirement of beneficial ownership).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg TP documentation law (Law of 28 December 2023): Master File/Local File mandatory where the MNE group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50 million AND the aggregate related-party transactions of the Luxembourg entity exceed EUR 1 million per fiscal year. The Local File must be delivered within 30 days after a request from the ACD; the Master File within 30 days. CbC Report threshold EUR 750 million group revenue. Penalty for deficient documentation: EUR 50,000 per document (Article 56 LIR), plus possible 10% revaluation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply ESR-type offshore legislation, but substance is mandatory: (1) Article 14 LIR — management and control (siège de direction effective) in Luxembourg; (2) General Anti-Abuse Rule (Article 6 StAnpG) and ATAD GAAR deny treaty/participation benefits where the arrangement is non-genuine; (3) EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive anti-abuse clause (12-month holding and subject-to-tax test); (4) FATF/AML substance for the bitumen wholesale business: local office, staff, warehouse/incoterm evidence, transport contracts, and trade documentation to avoid a finding of a nominee 'letterbox' operation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful submission of false Form 700 declarations, concealed cross-border bitumen trading income, fictitious invoices from shell suppliers, or false TP documentation understating taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years (Article 1733 AO and Article 496 et seq. Criminal Code); administrative 10% surcharge; late-payment interest at 0.6% monthly; denial of treaty benefits under the GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal liability of signatories: imprisonment of the managing director; personal asset seizure; travel ban and international arrest warrant issued by the investigating magistrate; civil claim by the tax administration in the criminal proceedings (partie civile) for restitution of the evaded tax plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Nominee-only directorship, no local employees or trading office in Luxembourg, invoices routed through the SARL without actual commercial activity, cash-flow only via third-party managed accounts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the Luxembourg seat of management and control; corporate residence reattributed to the parent jurisdiction; reclassification of the entity as transparent for CIT/net wealth tax; imposition of the 18% (formerly 15%) filing fine where no return; OECD/ATAD GAAR denies the EUR 50 million group thresholds and participation exemptions; possible de-registration from the RCS
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face 'faute de gestion' liability under Article 495-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 (action en comblement du passif) — joint civil liability for company debts including taxes where negligence caused insolvency; criminal charges for falsification of accounts; travel bans in proceedings for concealment of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing of bitumen purchases from affiliated refiners, excessive management or marketing fees paid to a related foreign entity, or year-end artificial reallocation of profit to a zero-rate jurisdiction without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 56 LIR, the ACD re-determines the taxable base at the arm's-length price; the taxpayer bears the burden of proof; adjustment of hidden profit distribution triggers 15% dividend WHT and solidarity surcharge; TP documentation failure: EUR 50,000 fine per missing document plus a 10% penalty on the re-assessed tax; interest at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The tax authority can name the director in the assessment order as a donee of the hidden distribution (transparent attribution), creating personal solidarity liability for the WHT shortfall; criminal referral for income tax evasion where the TP adjustment exceeds materiality thresholds; interdict (travel ban) on the director's private assets pending payment.
